purpose: Test whether anatomy-based inter-subject surface alignment improves cross-subject motor decoding over the frozen volumetric bounding-box rescale.

within_subject_leave_one_run_out.interpretation: Surface carries MORE information within subject (+0.042 SVM), so the cross-subject loss is a transfer failure, not information loss from the projection.

pipeline_verification.note: Checked before believing the negative result.
pipeline_verification.conclusion: MSMSulc registration is correctly applied and does improve anatomical correspondence over the unregistered sphere.

established: Surface projection preserves and slightly improves representation information content while transferring worse across subjects than a volumetric bounding-box rescale. Anatomical alignment of cortical folding is not sufficient to improve cross-subject motor decoding on this cohort.
not_established: Whether the deficit is because surface alignment adds nothing over bounding-box rescaling for functional correspondence, or because the discarded subcortex and cerebellum carry unusually cross-subject-consistent signal. The within-subject result weakens but does not eliminate the second. A ribbon-masked volumetric control separates them and must be run before the manuscript commits.
next: Connectivity hyperalignment. The dissociation (more signal, worse correspondence) is exactly the deficit functional alignment is designed to repair.

connectivity_hyperalignment.method: per-fold template from training subjects only; 324 parcels; orthogonal Procrustes on vertex-to-parcel connectivity profiles; 3 refinement iterations
connectivity_hyperalignment.leakage: No labels at any stage. Template rebuilt inside every fold so held-out subjects never shape the feature space. Each subject's rotation comes from their own unlabeled profile.

paired_test_linear_svm_independent.note: hyperaligned minus unaligned surface, paired per fold

connectivity_hyperalignment.interpretation: Functional alignment recovers a little over half the surface-to-volumetric transfer deficit (+0.033 of 0.059) using only label-free connectivity structure, confirming the deficit was genuinely a correspondence problem. It does not overtake the volumetric baseline: 0.7789 vs 0.8051. It harms the correlation classifier (-0.065) because per-parcel rotations fitted to noisy connectivity profiles add estimation noise a nearest-centroid classifier cannot discount.

residual_gap.candidate: the volumetric bounding box retains subcortex and cerebellum; the surface does not
residual_gap.decisive_test: ribbon-masked volumetric decoder — removes the coverage advantage while keeping everything else

combined_representation.question: Do volumetric and hyperaligned-surface features carry complementary information?
combined_representation.why_not_ribbon_mask: The direct ribbon-masked volumetric control needs every subject's surfaces and BOLD affines re-downloaded (~12GB) to label the 24^3 grid anatomically. Concatenation bounds the same question cheaply.
combined_representation.interpretation: The surface features demonstrably change predictions - no fold is unchanged and individual folds move by up to 0.058 - yet contribute exactly nothing on net. This is a null from active features, not inert ones.
combined_representation.strengthens: The coverage explanation. If the surface carried information the volumetric grid lacked, concatenation would capture it; the decoder is free to use both.
combined_representation.does_not_prove: That the residual gap IS coverage. The surface information could be a strict subset for reasons unrelated to which structures are included. The ribbon-masked control remains decisive.
combined_representation.practical: Surface alignment offers no route to a better headline number. The 0.8314 frozen result is not improved by adding a functionally aligned cortical surface representation.

radial_partition_probe.premise: Cortex lies peripherally in the bounding box, subcortex centrally; radial shells would separate them.
radial_partition_probe.premise_was_wrong: The signal is concentrated centrally. The outer 40% of the radius (6616 voxels, 48% of the grid) decodes near chance because those shells are largely OUTSIDE the brain - the transform rescales the bounding box of the whole imaged volume, so they contain skull, scalp and air. The partition separates brain from non-brain, not cortex from subcortex, and does not answer the coverage question.
surviving_findings: Nearly half the volumetric feature space is dead weight: the outer 48% of voxels contribute almost nothing, consistent with the signal living in many low-variance directions rather than leading components.

The central region alone (2176 voxels, 16% of the grid) supports 0.7411 - within 0.04 of the hyperaligned surface and 0.065 of full volumetric. Those voxels carry substantial class information a cortical surface cannot access.
radial_partition_probe.status: Consistent with the coverage explanation but not confirmation. 'Central in a bounding box' is not an anatomical label. The coverage explanation has now survived two cheap probes without being confirmed by either; the ribbon-masked control remains the decisive test.

ribbon_masked_control.how_it_became_affordable: Labelling the grid needs BOLD geometry, not BOLD data. A NIfTI header is 348 bytes, so a 64KB HTTP range request per subject yields shape and affine (verified against sub-01 vs the full 190MB file). Cost fell from ~12GB to ~870MB of surfaces plus 4MB of headers. This should have been checked before running two proxies that could not answer the question.
ribbon_masked_control.conclusion: Restricting the volumetric decoder to cortex does NOT cost accuracy - it slightly improves it (0.8177 vs 0.8051 at the 0.25 threshold). The volumetric advantage does not come from subcortex or cerebellum. The coverage hypothesis, which survived three probes, is refuted.
ribbon_masked_control.what_remains: Correspondence itself. The surface is more reliable (0.6665 vs 0.5983) and more informative within subject (0.7332 vs 0.6912); its cross-subject deficit is not coverage; and functional alignment recovers only half. For this task MSMSulc folding-based registration provides no cross-subject advantage over a bounding-box rescale. Cortical folding and somatotopic functional location evidently do not correspond tightly enough across subjects to pay for the resampling.
ribbon_masked_control.publishable_claim: On this cohort, anatomy-based surface normalisation does not improve cross-subject motor decoding, and a bounding-box rescale is a competitive alternative.

stacked_improvements.note: ANOVA selection and ensembling do not compound (+0.001 over ensemble alone), suggesting both are capturing the same noise reduction.
